messages.author: a11a7aeae7fef908
messages.subject: Problems Installing RStan
parts:
R version 3.20
Rtools version 3.3
RStudio version 0.99.446

Hi RStan Users,

As I switched to a newer computer, I have been reinstalling my systems and software applications, including RStan. But I am having problems installing RStan after several attemps. I've tried different versions of Rtools and R. During the installation, I was stopped to update loaded packages. In addition, while installing Rtools, I also checked the box for allowing editing the system PATH. I followed instructions posted on https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started.

Jun Xu, PhD
Associate Professor
Department of Sociology
Ball State University
Muncie, IN 47306

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Problems Installing RStan
parts:
On Friday, June 19, 2015 at 6:24:38 PM UTC-4, jun...@gmail.com wrote:
Error in install.packages : Updating loaded packages

Attaching package: ‘Rcpp’

You already had Rcpp loaded when it tried to update it, possibly due to an entry in .Rprofile or silently loading an .RData file that contained an object specific to Rcpp. If you run the install script again without first having loaded any packages, it should work.

Ben

When you open RStudio, what does

search()

say? If there is no Rcpp, RcppEigen, BH, and inline,  then that script should work without saying
Error in install.packages : Updating loaded packages

but you may have to remove some 00-LOCK folders from previous failed installations.

Ben

Ben,

You are right. I got several previous installations still floating around. After I cleaned them, rstan was installed successfully. This is my second time installing rstan (the first time was in 2013), and during both times, I had problems. I know this is asking a lot from stan people, but I wish the installation process could be further streamlined so that one line of code/r script would do all things. Thanks a lot!

Jun

messages.subject: Re: Problems Installing RStan
parts:
Once it is on CRAN, it won't be any harder to install than any other R package, but you still have to have a C++ compiler.

Ben

On Wednesday, June 24, 2015 at 7:21:50 AM UTC-4, jun...@gmail.com wrote:
Ben,

You are right. I got several previous installations still floating around. After I cleaned them, rstan was installed successfully. This is my second time installing rstan (the first time was in 2013), and during both times, I had problems. I know this is asking a lot from stan people, but I wish the installation process could be further streamlined so that one line of code/r script would do all things. Thanks a lot!

Jun
